decision: Use corridor-month as the modelling grain
rationale: Supports time-based forecasting and corridor-level planning

decision: Use 43 corridors as the initial candidate set
rationale: Maintains the confirmed project boundary while corridor geometry is verified
Random splitting would leak future information into model evaluation

decision: Treat budget and equity values as planning scenarios
rationale: No official City values have been verified for this project

decision: Keep final authority with the City and engineering teams
rationale: The analytical system is decision support and cannot replace feasibility review

decision: Preserve raw source files without manual modification
rationale: Reproducibility requires cleaning to occur only in interim and processed layers

decision: Use January 2018 through December 2025 as the candidate historical window
rationale: This provides exactly 96 citywide monthly periods while excluding incomplete 2017 coverage and partial 2026 data

decision: Use crashes.crash_date as the authoritative event timestamp after joining child sources
rationale: All child crash_record_id values matched the crash table but 148 vehicle rows and 161 people rows contained a different redundant crash_date value

decision: Use crashes as the parent table and left join vehicle and people enrichments
rationale: An inner join would incorrectly remove 1987 crash records that have no corresponding people row

decision: Persist every crash-cleaning run result and block output publication after critical validation failure
rationale: Data-quality failures must remain auditable and must not replace a previously valid analytical dataset

decision: Treat configured speed lane and unit plausibility thresholds as warning-only checks
rationale: Observed outliers may be source-quality issues but cleaning must preserve records for review

decision: Approve the validated crash core for spatial processing with documented limitations
rationale: Independent validation confirmed 877919 rows, exact schema, zero key date and derived-field errors, successful Day 5 reconciliation, and four warning-only quality issues

decision: Use Socrata backing dataset pr57-gg9e for Street Center Lines acquisition
rationale: The public map view 6imu-meau is a visualization layer whose legacy export returned an incomplete GeoJSON; the backing dataset returned 56338 paginated features.

decision: Preserve invalid street geometries in raw evidence but exclude them from corridor construction
rationale: Two of 56338 centerline features had empty geometries. Valid geometry coverage was 99.9964 percent, above the configured 99.9 percent acceptance threshold.

decision: Use page 9 as the canonical corridor-definition source and pages 27 through 29 for cross-reference validation
rationale: Page 9 defines all 43 corridors while pages 27 through 29 confirm endpoints, 23 directional reversals, 16 continuous sub-segment chains, and zero endpoint disagreements

decision: Approve three exception routing policies for corridor geometry construction
rationale: Policy B (Lake Shore Drive two-carriageway MultiLineString with 200ft proximity tolerance), Policy C (Fairbanks/Columbus source continuation), Policy D (Wacker multilevel source family). Note that the 200ft boundary tolerance is strictly for centerline endpoint resolution and is not the crash-assignment threshold.
